description: Process a data subject request (access, deletion, correction, portability) from intake through fulfillment to response within legal deadlines.

steps.description: Receive a data subject request and verify the identity of the requester.

inputs.name: request-details
inputs.desc: The data subject request including type (access, deletion, correction, portability) and requester information

inputs.name: applicable-regulations
inputs.desc: The privacy regulations that apply (GDPR, CCPA, state laws)

outputs.name: verified-request
outputs.desc: The validated request with confirmed requester identity

outputs.name: request-type
outputs.desc: The classified request type and applicable deadline

process: Log the request with a unique tracking number and timestamp.
Verify the requester's identity using available information (account match, government ID, knowledge-based verification).
Classify the request type (access, deletion, correction, portability) and determine the legal deadline for response.
Acknowledge receipt to the requester within the required timeframe.

steps.description: Locate all personal data belonging to the data subject across systems.

inputs.name: verified-request
inputs.desc: The validated request with confirmed identity

inputs.name: request-type
inputs.desc: The type of request being processed

outputs.name: data-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete inventory of the data subject's personal data across all systems

outputs.name: system-list
outputs.desc: List of systems containing the data subject's data

process: Query the data map to identify all systems that may contain the data subject's personal data.
Search each system for records matching the data subject's identifiers (email, name, account ID).
Compile the inventory of data found, organized by system and data category.
Flag any systems where data could not be searched automatically for manual review.

steps.description: Execute the requested action (export, delete, correct) across all systems.

inputs.name: data-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of personal data across systems

inputs.name: request-type
inputs.desc: The type of action to perform

outputs.name: fulfillment-log
outputs.desc: Record of actions taken in each system (exported, deleted, corrected)

outputs.name: exceptions
outputs.desc: Any data that could not be processed and the reason (legal hold, regulatory retention)

process: For access or portability requests, export the data in a machine-readable format.
For deletion requests, delete or anonymize the data in each system, respecting legal retention requirements.
For correction requests, update the data in each system and verify the correction.
Log each action taken, the system affected, and the timestamp.
Document any exceptions where data was retained and the legal basis for retention.

steps.description: Prepare and send the formal response to the data subject.

inputs.name: exceptions
inputs.desc: Data that could not be processed and reasons

outputs.name: response-letter
outputs.desc: The formal response sent to the data subject

outputs.name: dsr-record
outputs.desc: The complete DSR record for audit purposes

process: Draft the response letter summarizing the actions taken and any exceptions.
For access or portability requests, package the exported data securely for delivery.
Send the response to the data subject through a secure channel.
File the complete DSR record (request, verification, actions, response) for audit retention.

description: Set up a consent management system: inventory collection points, define consent categories, implement the consent mechanism, and honor consent across systems.

steps.description: Inventory all points where personal data is collected from individuals.

inputs.name: organization-context
inputs.desc: Description of the organization and its data collection activities

inputs.name: digital-properties
inputs.desc: List of websites, apps, and other digital properties

outputs.name: collection-point-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete list of data collection points (web forms, app screens, phone, in-person, third-party)

outputs.name: data-purposes
outputs.desc: The purposes for which data is collected at each point

process: List all digital properties (websites, mobile apps, web apps) and their data collection forms.
Identify offline collection points (phone, in-person, paper forms, events).
Document the data types collected and the stated purpose at each point.
Note any third-party collection (analytics scripts, advertising pixels, embedded content).

steps.description: Define the consent categories and their legal basis.

inputs.name: collection-point-inventory
inputs.desc: The inventory of data collection points

outputs.name: consent-categories
outputs.desc: Defined consent categories (necessary, preferences, analytics, marketing) with descriptions

outputs.name: legal-basis-mapping
outputs.desc: Mapping of each data processing activity to its legal basis

process: Group data processing activities into consent categories (strictly necessary, functional preferences, analytics and performance, marketing and advertising).
Determine the legal basis for each category (consent, legitimate interest, contractual necessity, legal obligation).
Write the user-facing descriptions for each category in plain language.
Define which categories require opt-in versus opt-out under the applicable regulations.

steps.description: Implement the consent collection mechanism (banner, preference center).

inputs.name: legal-basis-mapping
inputs.desc: Legal basis for each processing activity

outputs.name: consent-mechanism-spec
outputs.desc: Specification of the consent banner and preference center design

outputs.name: implementation-checklist
outputs.desc: Checklist of technical requirements for consent collection and enforcement

process: Design the consent banner (first visit experience, category toggles, accept/reject buttons).
Design the preference center where users can review and change consent at any time.
Define the technical behavior: block non-essential scripts until consent is given, re-check on consent change.
Specify the consent record format (timestamp, categories, version, user ID).

steps.description: Configure consent signals to propagate across all systems that process personal data.

outputs.name: propagation-architecture
outputs.desc: How consent signals flow from collection to all downstream systems

outputs.name: consent-management-document
outputs.desc: The complete consent management setup document

process: Map the consent signal flow from the collection point to each downstream system (CRM, email platform, analytics, advertising).
Configure each system to check consent status before processing data for non-essential purposes.
Set up the consent change workflow: when a user revokes consent, trigger the appropriate actions in each system.
Document the consent management setup for audit and compliance review.

description: Audit a website's cookie and tracker compliance: scan, classify, verify consent enforcement, and fix violations.

steps.description: Scan a website to identify all cookies, trackers, and scripts that process user data.

inputs.name: website-url
inputs.desc: The URL of the website to scan

inputs.name: scan-scope
inputs.desc: Pages to scan (all, top-level, specific paths)

outputs.name: cookie-inventory
outputs.desc: List of all cookies found (name, domain, expiry, type, value pattern)

outputs.name: tracker-inventory
outputs.desc: List of all third-party trackers and scripts detected

process: Crawl the specified pages and record all cookies set (first-party and third-party).
Detect all third-party scripts, pixels, and trackers loaded on each page.
Record the cookie attributes (name, domain, path, expiry, secure flag, SameSite).
Identify any cookies set before the user interacts with the consent mechanism.

steps.description: Classify each cookie and tracker by category and purpose.

outputs.name: classified-cookies
outputs.desc: Each cookie classified into a category (necessary, preferences, analytics, marketing) with a stated purpose

outputs.name: unknown-cookies
outputs.desc: Cookies that could not be automatically classified for manual review

process: Match each cookie against known cookie databases to identify its purpose and owner.
Classify each cookie into a consent category (strictly necessary, functional, analytics, advertising).
Flag any cookies that cannot be automatically classified for manual review.
Verify that the classifications match the categories declared in the consent banner.

steps.description: Test that non-essential cookies are blocked until the user gives consent.

outputs.name: enforcement-results
outputs.desc: Results of testing consent enforcement (pass/fail for each cookie category)

outputs.name: violations
outputs.desc: List of cookies that fire before consent is given

process: Load the website without interacting with the consent banner and record which cookies are set.
Verify that only strictly necessary cookies are present before consent.
Accept each category individually and verify that only the corresponding cookies are activated.
Reject all optional categories and verify that no non-essential cookies are set.

steps.description: Fix identified cookie compliance violations and produce the audit report.

inputs.name: violations
inputs.desc: List of cookies that violate consent rules

outputs.name: remediation-actions
outputs.desc: Actions taken to fix each violation

outputs.name: cookie-audit-report
outputs.desc: The complete cookie compliance audit report

process: For each violation, determine the fix (block script until consent, remove unnecessary cookie, recategorize).
Update the consent management platform configuration to enforce the correct blocking.
Re-test to confirm all violations are resolved.
Produce the cookie audit report with findings, remediation actions, and the current compliance status.

description: Map personal data flows across the organization to produce a Record of Processing Activities (ROPA).

steps.description: Inventory all processing activities that involve personal data.

inputs.name: organization-description
inputs.desc: Description of the organization, departments, and business activities

inputs.name: existing-documentation
inputs.desc: Any existing data inventories, privacy policies, or data flow diagrams

outputs.name: processing-activities
outputs.desc: List of all processing activities with description, department, and data subjects involved

outputs.name: system-inventory
outputs.desc: List of all systems (applications, databases, SaaS tools) that process personal data

process: Interview each department or review existing documentation to identify processing activities.
For each activity, record the description, responsible department, and categories of data subjects.
Inventory the systems used for each activity (applications, databases, cloud services, spreadsheets).
Note any processing performed by third-party processors on behalf of the organization.

steps.description: Catalog the data elements, purposes, legal bases, and retention periods for each processing activity.

outputs.name: data-catalog
outputs.desc: Catalog of data elements per activity (categories, sensitivity, purpose, legal basis, retention)

outputs.name: third-party-recipients
outputs.desc: List of third parties receiving personal data and the purpose of each transfer

process: For each processing activity, list the personal data categories collected (name, email, financial, health, biometric).
Document the purpose for each data category and the legal basis (consent, contract, legitimate interest, legal obligation).
Set the retention period for each data category based on legal requirements and business need.
Identify all third-party recipients and document the transfer mechanism (DPA, SCCs, adequacy decision).

steps.description: Map the data flows between systems, departments, and third parties.

outputs.name: data-flow-diagram
outputs.desc: Visual and textual representation of how personal data moves through the organization

outputs.name: cross-border-transfers
outputs.desc: List of data transfers outside the jurisdiction with the legal mechanism used

process: Draw the data flows from collection point through internal systems to storage and deletion.
Mark all transfers to third parties and cross-border transfers.
Identify the security measures applied at each stage (encryption in transit, at rest, access controls).
Flag any flows that lack a documented legal basis or security measure.

steps.description: Compile the Record of Processing Activities (ROPA) and identify gaps.

outputs.name: ropa-document
outputs.desc: The completed Record of Processing Activities

outputs.name: gap-report
outputs.desc: Gaps identified (missing legal basis, missing DPA, excessive retention, undocumented flows)

process: Compile the ROPA in the required format (controller name, purposes, data categories, recipients, transfers, retention, security measures).
Review each entry for completeness and flag gaps (missing legal basis, missing data processing agreement, no retention period set).
Prioritize the gaps by risk level.
Produce the ROPA document and the gap report with recommended remediation actions.

description: Conduct a privacy-by-design review for a new product, feature, or system before launch.

steps.description: Describe the planned data processing for the new product or feature.

inputs.name: feature-description
inputs.desc: Description of the new product, feature, or system

inputs.name: technical-design
inputs.desc: Technical design documents or architecture diagrams

outputs.name: processing-summary
outputs.desc: Summary of all personal data processing involved (what data, why, how, where, how long)

outputs.name: data-subjects
outputs.desc: Categories of individuals whose data will be processed

process: Describe the feature and its purpose in plain language.
List all personal data that will be collected, generated, or inferred.
Document how the data flows through the system (collection, processing, storage, sharing, deletion).
Identify the categories of data subjects affected (users, employees, partners, minors).

steps.description: Identify the privacy risks in the planned processing.

outputs.name: risk-register
outputs.desc: List of identified privacy risks with likelihood and impact assessment

outputs.name: high-risk-flags
outputs.desc: Processing activities that may trigger a DPIA requirement

process: Assess each processing activity against the privacy principles (minimization, purpose limitation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity, confidentiality).
Identify risks to data subjects (unauthorized access, data breach, function creep, profiling, discrimination).
Rate each risk by likelihood and impact.
Flag any processing that meets the criteria for a mandatory Data Protection Impact Assessment.

steps.description: Recommend privacy-enhancing measures to mitigate the identified risks.

outputs.name: recommended-measures
outputs.desc: Privacy-enhancing measures to mitigate each risk

outputs.name: design-changes
outputs.desc: Specific changes to the technical design to embed privacy

process: For each risk, identify the appropriate mitigation (data minimization, pseudonymization, encryption, access controls, retention limits, anonymization).
Recommend specific design changes (collect less data, shorter retention, user controls, audit logging).
Assess the residual risk after applying each measure.
Prioritize the measures by effectiveness and implementation effort.

steps.description: Document the privacy-by-design review and its outcomes.

outputs.name: review-record
outputs.desc: The documented privacy-by-design review

outputs.name: implementation-requirements
outputs.desc: Privacy requirements that must be met before launch

process: Compile the review record (processing description, risks, measures, design changes, residual risk).
List the privacy requirements that must be implemented before launch.
Obtain sign-off from the privacy team and the product owner.
Schedule the post-launch review to verify that the measures are working as intended.

description: Manage a personal data breach from assessment through regulatory notification to individual notification.

steps.description: Assess the scope and severity of the data breach.

inputs.name: incident-report
inputs.desc: The initial incident report describing the breach

outputs.name: breach-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of the breach (data types, volume, number of individuals, risk of harm)

outputs.name: notification-determination
outputs.desc: Whether regulatory and individual notification is required under applicable law

process: Determine what personal data was compromised (categories, sensitivity, volume).
Estimate the number of affected individuals and their jurisdictions.
Assess the risk of harm to individuals (identity theft, financial loss, discrimination, reputational damage).
Determine whether regulatory notification is required (risk threshold, mandatory reporting) and the applicable deadlines.

steps.description: Prepare and submit the notification to the relevant regulatory authority.

inputs.name: breach-assessment
inputs.desc: The breach scope and severity assessment

outputs.name: regulatory-notification
outputs.desc: The notification submitted to the regulator

outputs.name: submission-record
outputs.desc: Record of submission (date, method, confirmation)

process: Draft the regulatory notification with the required information (nature of breach, data categories, number of individuals, consequences, measures taken).
Have the notification reviewed by legal counsel.
Submit the notification to the supervisory authority within the legal deadline (72 hours for GDPR).
Record the submission details (date, method, reference number, confirmation receipt).

steps.description: Notify the affected individuals about the breach.

inputs.name: regulatory-notification
inputs.desc: What was reported to the regulator

outputs.name: individual-notification
outputs.desc: The notification sent to affected individuals

outputs.name: delivery-record
outputs.desc: Record of notification delivery (method, date, count)

process: Draft the individual notification in plain language (what happened, what data was affected, what we are doing, what they should do).
Select the delivery method (email, letter, website notice) based on the number of individuals and contact information available.
Send the notification to all affected individuals.
Set up a support channel (phone, email, FAQ page) for questions from affected individuals.

steps.description: Conduct the post-incident review and produce the breach record.

outputs.name: post-incident-report
outputs.desc: Post-incident review with root cause, timeline, and lessons learned

outputs.name: breach-notification-record
outputs.desc: The complete breach notification record for compliance archives

process: Conduct a post-incident review to identify the root cause and contributing factors.
Document the complete timeline from detection to notification.
Identify remediation actions to prevent recurrence.
Compile the complete breach notification record (assessment, notifications, responses, remediation) for the compliance archive.

description: Assess a vendor's privacy practices before sharing personal data with them.

steps.description: Send the privacy assessment questionnaire to the vendor.

inputs.name: vendor-name
inputs.desc: Name of the vendor being assessed

inputs.name: data-sharing-scope
inputs.desc: Description of what personal data will be shared and for what purpose

outputs.name: questionnaire-responses
outputs.desc: The vendor's completed privacy questionnaire

outputs.name: vendor-documentation
outputs.desc: Supporting documentation provided by the vendor (privacy policy, certifications, audit reports)

process: Select the appropriate questionnaire based on the data sensitivity and processing scope.
Send the questionnaire to the vendor with a deadline for completion.
Request supporting documentation (privacy policy, SOC 2 report, ISO 27001 certificate, data processing agreement template).
Follow up if responses are incomplete or unclear.

steps.description: Evaluate the vendor's privacy practices based on their responses and documentation.

outputs.name: privacy-risk-score
outputs.desc: Risk rating for the vendor's privacy practices (low, medium, high)

outputs.name: findings
outputs.desc: Specific findings (strengths and gaps in the vendor's privacy practices)

process: Review the vendor's data protection measures (encryption, access controls, data segregation, backup).
Assess the vendor's breach response capability (detection, notification timeline, remediation).
Evaluate the vendor's sub-processor management (list of sub-processors, approval process, oversight).
Review the vendor's data retention and deletion practices.
Score the vendor's overall privacy risk level.

steps.description: Negotiate the data processing agreement with the vendor.

outputs.name: dpa-terms
outputs.desc: Agreed data processing agreement terms

outputs.name: remediation-requirements
outputs.desc: Conditions the vendor must meet before data sharing begins

process: Draft or review the data processing agreement covering processing scope, security measures, breach notification, audit rights, sub-processor controls, and data return/deletion.
Negotiate any terms where the vendor's standard agreement falls below requirements.
Define any remediation actions the vendor must complete before data sharing begins.
Obtain signatures from both parties.

steps.description: Produce the vendor privacy assessment report and file the record.

outputs.name: assessment-report
outputs.desc: The vendor privacy assessment report with risk rating, findings, and conditions

outputs.name: vendor-privacy-record
outputs.desc: The filed assessment record for ongoing monitoring

process: Compile the assessment report (vendor profile, scope, risk score, findings, DPA terms, conditions).
Record the approval or rejection decision with rationale.
Schedule the reassessment date based on risk level (annually for high risk, biennially for low).
File the record in the vendor management system.

description: Build and deploy a privacy training program for the organization.

steps.description: Identify the training audiences and their privacy knowledge requirements.

inputs.name: organization-context
inputs.desc: Description of the organization and its data processing activities

inputs.name: regulatory-requirements
inputs.desc: Applicable privacy regulations and their training mandates

outputs.name: training-audiences
outputs.desc: Defined training audiences (all staff, data handlers, IT, developers, leadership) with their specific needs

outputs.name: knowledge-requirements
outputs.desc: The privacy topics each audience must understand

process: Identify the training audiences based on their role in data processing (general awareness, data handlers, privacy team, developers, leadership).

Define the knowledge requirements for each audience (general: what is personal data, rights, reporting; handlers: classification, retention, access; developers: privacy by design, minimization, security).
Review regulatory training requirements (GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA mandates) to ensure coverage.
Set the training frequency (onboarding, annual refresh, role change).

steps.description: Develop the training content for each audience.

outputs.name: training-modules
outputs.desc: The training modules for each audience (content, format, duration)

outputs.name: assessment-questions
outputs.desc: Knowledge check questions for each module

process: Write the training content for each module using real-world scenarios relevant to the organization.
Select the format for each module (online self-paced, live workshop, video, interactive scenario).
Create the knowledge check questions to verify comprehension.
Review the content with the privacy team for accuracy.

steps.description: Deploy the training to all target audiences and track completion.

outputs.name: deployment-schedule
outputs.desc: The rollout schedule by audience and deadline

outputs.name: completion-tracking
outputs.desc: Tracking of completion rates and assessment scores by audience

process: Load the training modules into the learning management system or distribution platform.
Assign the modules to each audience with a completion deadline.
Send reminders to employees who have not completed by the midpoint.
Track completion rates and assessment pass rates.
Escalate non-completion to managers as the deadline approaches.

steps.description: Review the training program effectiveness and plan improvements.

outputs.name: effectiveness-report
outputs.desc: Report on training completion, assessment scores, and knowledge gaps

outputs.name: privacy-training-program-document
outputs.desc: The complete privacy training program document for compliance records

process: Analyze completion rates by audience and department.
Review assessment scores to identify common knowledge gaps.
Gather participant feedback on content relevance and format.
Recommend improvements for the next training cycle.
Produce the privacy training program document for compliance archives.
